fact: Finance Minister Ngafuan cited reforms involving e-procurement among Liberia's partnerships and reforms, in a speech reported 2026-09-28.

The Liberian Observer reports the President formally launched the national e-GP system in February 2025, after a six-institution pilot; businesses register, bid and manage contracts on it, and Sierra Leone's procurement authority studied it in August 2026 as a working, deployed system.

PPCC says 56 government procurement entities are already onboarded onto the e-GP platform, as Phase II of its nationwide rollout began on 11 May 2026, with training on provider registration, annual procurement planning, e-notification, invitations and electronic bidding.

Tech Africa News reports the PPCC's e-GP system lets government institutions plan, advertise, evaluate and award procurement contracts digitally, replacing the manual process; more than 1,200 vendors are registered and the platform has raised more than US$400,000 in fees.

The Public Procurement and Concessions Commission says its Electronic Government Procurement (e-GP) system has six early-adopter bodies and 127 live processes, with 50 more ministries, agencies and commissions to be onboarded.
The Commission reports 127 live processes on the e-GP system, with 494 vendors and 155 users trained.
President Boakai launched the Electronic Government Procurement (e-GP) System on 6 February 2025, already rolled out in six government agencies with over 200 enrolled businesses, for online bidding.
President Boakai mandated use of the e-GP System by all government procuring entities when launching it on 6 February 2025.

PPCC Executive Director Bodger Scott Johnson says Liberia's Electronic Government Procurement (e-GP) system, developed with European Dynamics, is in use, with 50 more ministries, agencies and commissions being trained for onboarding.
The PPCC head says with e-GP every stage of procurement, from planning to contract award, is tracked digitally.
The PPCC head says more than US$28 million in contracts have been awarded to Liberian-owned businesses through e-GP.
The Ministry of Information's PPCC overview says Liberia's e-GP system, launched in February 2025 with a pilot of six procuring entities, is fully functional.
The PPCC overview says the e-GP system has recorded 132 procurement transactions and registered 543 vendors.

PPCC executive director Bodger Scott Johnson said on 2025-09-23 that the e-GP system, launched in February 2025, runs all procurement of six government entities, with 50 more to be onboarded by the next fiscal year.

PPCC executive director Bodger Scott Johnson said contracts worth US$12,219,000 had been awarded through the e-GP system, including 27 by the Liberia Revenue Authority, 19 by Public Works, 17 by PPCC, 10 by Finance and 7 by Education.

The Public Procurement and Concessions Commission's 2024 report says the World Bank-funded e-GP system went live in 2024 as a pilot in six entities (finance, health, public works, education ministries, the revenue authority and the Commission), with enrolment of 50 more entities expected.
